keyVerseText: For that is his covering only, it is his raiment for his skin: wherein shall he sleep? and it shall come to pass, when he crieth unto me, that I will hear; for I am gracious.
rootMeaning: The root of חַנּוּן (channûwn) is חָנַן (chânan), which conveys the idea of bending or stooping in kindness toward someone inferior. This root meaning adds depth to the common English gloss 'gracious' by emphasizing an active, compassionate disposition that involves favor and mercy extended intentionally and humbly. It is not merely a passive attribute but a dynamic expression of kindness and mercy toward those in need.
usageInScripture: The word חַנּוּן appears thirteen times in the Old Testament, consistently used as an attribute of God. It is often paired with רַחוּם (rachûwm), meaning 'merciful,' highlighting God's compassionate nature. Translations vary slightly but center on the concept of grace and favor, such as 'and gracious,' 'is gracious,' and 'for I am gracious,' demonstrating a steady emphasis on God's readiness to show kindness and hear the cries of the vulnerable.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding חַנּוּן as God's gracious character is vital for grasping the biblical portrayal of divine mercy and covenant faithfulness. It reveals a God who is not distant or indifferent but actively inclined to show compassion and respond to human need. This graciousness undergirds the gospel message, pointing to the unmerited favor God extends through Christ. Recognizing God's חַנּוּן invites believers to trust in His mercy and to reflect that same gracious spirit in their relationships.
keyVerseReflection: Exodus 22:27 states, 'when he crieth unto me, that I will hear; for I am gracious.' Here, חַנּוּן underscores God's compassionate response to the cries of the oppressed or needy. The verse illustrates that God's graciousness is not abstract but is manifested in His attentive care and willingness to hear and provide for those who call on Him. This assures believers of God's personal and gracious involvement in their distress.
